experiments.name: Exact-description novelty
experiments.research_question: Can exact novelty in verbalised event descriptions separate attack events without learning a statistical model?
experiments.hypothesis: A purely novelty-based rule will over-alert because most attack-test descriptions are also present in benign training data.
experiments.representation: V2 full-provenance event description (operations, entities and directed relationships)
experiments.training_strategy: Memorise the set of 13,029 unique training descriptions.
experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.897235 and Average Precision 0.003367. All 70 original positives were flagged, but 20,722 false positives produced precision of 0.337%.
experiments.interpretation: Description novelty alone captures some attack signal, but 79.39% of attack-test descriptions were seen in training, so novelty is a weak discriminator.
experiments.limitations: Binary scoring creates large tied blocks; the rule has no notion of semantic similarity.

experiments.name: TF-IDF with Isolation Forest
experiments.research_question: Does a sparse lexical representation with Isolation Forest provide a competitive anomaly baseline?
experiments.hypothesis: TF-IDF captures token-level rarity but will struggle with semantically equivalent descriptions.
experiments.representation: TF-IDF over 1-2 word n-grams of the V2 description
experiments.training_strategy: Fit vectoriser and Isolation Forest on 99,665 benign training events only.
experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.671003 and Average Precision 0.001274. At the P99 validation threshold, zero original positives and 1,445 false positives were flagged.
experiments.interpretation: Lexical rarity is a poor proxy for malicious semantics in this representation; ranking is only modestly above chance.
experiments.limitations: TF-IDF ignores word order and semantic similarity, and max_features truncates the vocabulary.

experiments.name: MiniLM with PCA reconstruction
experiments.research_question: Can linear subspace reconstruction of frozen MiniLM embeddings identify unusual events?
experiments.hypothesis: PCA reconstruction will capture dominant benign variation but miss nonlinear anomalies.
experiments.training_strategy: Fit PCA on benign training embeddings only.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction error

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.954165 and Average Precision 0.007092. All 70 original positives were detected with 10,778 false positives at P99.
experiments.interpretation: Semantic embeddings improve ranking over lexical baselines, but linear compression produces a weak anomaly score and low precision.
experiments.limitations: PCA is a linear method and its 32 components explain most benign variance, including possibly some attack signal.

experiments.name: MiniLM with Isolation Forest
experiments.research_question: Does Isolation Forest on frozen semantic embeddings outperform linear reconstruction?
experiments.hypothesis: Tree-based isolation may capture nonlinear embedding outliers better than PCA.
experiments.training_strategy: Fit Isolation Forest on benign training embeddings only.
experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.918413 and Average Precision 0.003858. Only 1 of 70 original positives was detected at P99, with 1,841 false positives.
experiments.interpretation: Isolation Forest ranks many attack events highly but the validation-calibrated threshold is poorly aligned with the attack distribution.
experiments.limitations: The P99 threshold from benign validation yields almost no recall; the result is highly operating-point dependent.

experiments.name: Operation-frequency baseline
experiments.research_question: How much detection signal is available from operation-name frequency alone?
experiments.hypothesis: Operation-only frequency will be weak because operation sequences are highly repetitive.
experiments.training_strategy: Estimate training operation-sequence frequencies; score unseen or rare sequences higher.
experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.826134 and Average Precision 0.003212. Zero original positives were detected at P99.
experiments.interpretation: Operation frequency alone provides weak ranking and no recall at the calibrated threshold.
experiments.limitations: This is the reference baseline for the E5 operation-only representation and inherits its ambiguity.

experiments.name: Original frequency-preserving autoencoder
experiments.research_question: Can a benign-trained autoencoder over frozen MiniLM embeddings detect anomalous provenance events?
experiments.hypothesis: A bottleneck autoencoder will assign higher reconstruction error to events unlike benign training activity.
experiments.training_strategy: Frequency-preserving training on all 99,665 benign training events.
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Best benign validation reconstruction loss; checkpoint restored at best epoch 65.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.984482 and Average Precision 0.020832. At P99, 70/70 original positives were detected with 11,332 false positives; contextual recall 100%.
experiments.interpretation: The autoencoder substantially improves anomaly ranking over baselines, but absolute precision remains low.
experiments.limitations: Single seed; severe class imbalance; threshold calibrated only on benign validation data.

experiments.name: Unique-description training
experiments.research_question: Does deduplicating benign training descriptions reduce frequency dominance and improve anomaly ranking?
experiments.hypothesis: Training on unique descriptions will prevent the most frequent template from dominating the reconstruction objective.
experiments.training_strategy: Unique-description training: one sample per distinct benign description (13,029 samples).
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Best benign validation reconstruction loss; checkpoint restored at best epoch 99.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.987755 and Average Precision 0.026071. At P99, 70/70 original positives were detected with 5,407 false positives; contextual recall 50.67%.
experiments.interpretation: Deduplication improves ranking and reduces false positives relative to E2-A, but contextual recall falls sharply.
experiments.limitations: Unique sampling discards frequency information; single seed; no independent validation scenario.

experiments.name: Frequency-weighted training
experiments.research_question: Does down-weighting frequent descriptions improve the benign reconstruction objective?
experiments.hypothesis: Frequency weighting with 1/sqrt(frequency) will balance learning without discarding repeated benign behaviour.
experiments.training_strategy: Frequency-preserving samples with per-description weight 1/sqrt(frequency).
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Best benign validation reconstruction loss; checkpoint restored at best epoch 42.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.983191 and Average Precision 0.019920. At P99, 70/70 original positives were detected with 10,189 false positives; contextual recall 99.11%.
experiments.interpretation: Frequency weighting retains recall but does not improve ranking over the original frequency-preserving model.
experiments.limitations: Single seed; weighting formula was not tuned; results are sensitive to threshold choice.

experiments.name: Approximately matched-update unique-description training
experiments.research_question: Can unique-description training be matched to the original optimiser-update budget while improving anomaly prioritisation?
experiments.hypothesis: Approximately matching the number of optimiser updates will provide a fair comparison between frequency-preserving and unique-description training.
experiments.training_strategy: Unique descriptions with approximately 25,350 optimiser updates (51 batches x 497 epochs).
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Best benign validation reconstruction loss over the matched update budget; best checkpoint at update 24,429.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors (primary operating point)
evaluation_configuration.exploratory_threshold: P99.95 analysed retrospectively after inspecting attack-test results

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.995584 and Average Precision 0.109080 — the leading observed anomaly ranking. At P99: 70/70 original positives, 8,628 false positives, contextual recall 77.33%. At P99.95: 70/70, 2,339 false positives, contextual recall 49.33%.
experiments.interpretation: Matched-update unique-description training is the strongest observed anomaly ranker and the best alert-prioritisation model, while precision remains low in absolute terms.
experiments.limitations: Single seed; the P99.95 threshold was inspected retrospectively and is not independently validated; no deployment threshold is claimed.

experiments.name: Threshold sensitivity analysis
experiments.research_question: How do precision, recall, false positives and contextual recall change across validation-derived thresholds?
experiments.hypothesis: Higher percentiles will reduce false positives at the cost of contextual recall, while original positive recall may remain high.
experiments.algorithm: Percentile sweep over benign validation reconstruction errors
experiments.training_strategy: Analytical study; no additional model training.
experiments.results_summary: For E2-D, P99 yields 70 TP / 8,628 FP and 77.33% contextual recall; P99.95 yields 70 TP / 2,339 FP and 49.33% contextual recall.
experiments.interpretation: Threshold choice strongly trades false-positive volume against contextual recall; P99 remains the primary experimental operating point.
experiments.limitations: P99.95 and related high-percentile points are retrospective diagnostics, not independently validated operating points.

experiments.name: Alert prioritisation analysis
experiments.research_question: How many original positives are recovered under fixed analyst alert budgets?
experiments.hypothesis: Better anomaly ranking will recover more positives within small alert budgets.
experiments.algorithm: Ranked alert-budget simulation with tie-aware expected TP
experiments.training_strategy: Analytical study; no additional model training.

evaluation_configuration.tie_handling: expected, minimum and maximum true positives

experiments.results_summary: E2-D recovers 46 of 70 original positives within the top 500 alerts and 58 within the top 1,000. E2-A, E2-B and E2-C recover 0, 7 and 0 respectively at 500.
experiments.interpretation: E2-D provides materially better analyst prioritisation, but absolute precision within small budgets remains low.
experiments.limitations: Measured only at the listed budgets; results depend on the single available seed and original annotation completeness.

experiments.name: Provenance ablation — operation only
experiments.research_question: How much detection signal remains when only system operation names are represented?
experiments.hypothesis: Operation-only representations will be highly ambiguous because many benign and malicious events share the same operation sequence.
experiments.representation: Operation-only description (operation names without entity attributes or relationships)
experiments.training_strategy: Frequency-preserving training on 99,665 benign operation-only descriptions.
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Fixed 100-epoch budget with no early stopping; best validation checkpoint retained.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.826367 and Average Precision 0.003219. Zero original positives and 618 false positives at P99; contextual recall 10.22%.
experiments.interpretation: Operation-only representations exhibit substantial ambiguity, with all 70 original positives sharing a description with 8,393 negatively labelled events.
experiments.limitations: The representation cannot distinguish events that differ only in entities or graph structure.

experiments.name: Provenance ablation — operations and entities
experiments.research_question: Do entity attributes resolve operation-only ambiguity without explicit directed relationships?
experiments.hypothesis: Adding process and artifact attributes will eliminate observed description conflicts and improve detection.
experiments.representation: Operations plus process and artifact attributes, without explicit directed relationships
experiments.training_strategy: Frequency-preserving training on 99,665 benign entity-enriched descriptions.
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Fixed 100-epoch budget with no early stopping; best validation checkpoint retained.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.982755 and Average Precision 0.018724. At P99: 70/70 original positives, 11,098 false positives, contextual recall 100%.
experiments.interpretation: Entity attributes eliminate observed exact-description conflicts for original positives and produce a large detection improvement over operation-only representations.
experiments.limitations: The representation does not encode explicit directed provenance relationships.

experiments.name: Provenance ablation — full provenance
experiments.research_question: Do explicit directed provenance relationships add detection value beyond operations and entity attributes?
experiments.hypothesis: Full provenance will improve observed Average Precision relative to the entity-based representation.
experiments.representation: Operations, entity attributes and explicit directed provenance relationships
experiments.training_strategy: Frequency-preserving training on 99,665 benign full-provenance descriptions.
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Fixed 100-epoch budget with no early stopping; best validation checkpoint retained.

evaluation_configuration.threshold: 99th percentile of benign validation reconstruction errors

experiments.results_summary: ROC-AUC 0.985507 and Average Precision 0.021743 — approximately 16.1% higher AP than E5-B. At P99: 70/70 original positives, 11,236 false positives, contextual recall 100%.
experiments.interpretation: Full provenance achieves the best observed AP among the E5 configurations, but it does not outperform the entity-based representation on every threshold-based metric.
experiments.limitations: The ablation measures overall representation differences, not exclusively the causal contribution of graph relationships; text ordering and formatting also differ.

experiments.name: Multiple-seed reproducibility
experiments.research_question: Do the observed experimental improvements remain consistent across different random seeds?
experiments.hypothesis: The E2-D ranking advantage will persist across seeds, but absolute metrics will vary.
experiments.training_strategy: Repeat the selected configurations with seeds 42, 123 and 456; report mean, standard deviation and individual outcomes.
experiments.checkpoint_selection: Same benign-validation checkpoint rule as the original experiment.
experiments.results_summary: Not yet executed.
experiments.interpretation: Current results are single-seed and should not be treated as stable estimates.
experiments.limitations: No multi-seed evidence exists yet.
